title: Storms roll through Piedmont Triad, cause flooding - NewsBreak
text: PIEDMONT TRIAD, N.C. (WGHP) — Storms are rolling through the Piedmont Triad. A flood watch will be in effect until 2 a.m. on Thursday for Alamance, Caswell, Davidson, Forsyth, Guilford, Montgomery, Randolph and Rockingham Counties. Communities that were affected by flash flooding earlier this week may be more prone to flash flooding tonight. Greensboro drivers are asked to be cautious around Battleground Avenue and Cotswald Avenue since a tree fell on power lines. Police are reporting some traffic light outages across Greensboro as well. The High Point Fire Department has reported multiple water rescues. FOX8 is told roads are also flooded in southwest High Point and in the Westchester Drive area. The Davidson County Sheriff’s Office said deputies are seeing flooding along Old Thomasville Road at Midway School Road. Flooding has been reported on Jacob Street as well. Use NOAA weather radio and/or the FOX8 MAX Weather app to get notified if warnings are issued in your area. Showers and thunderstorms are expected to taper off before midnight, but the flash flood threat is going to linger into the early morning hours. Afternoon showers and thunderstorms remain in the forecast for the rest of the week, the weekend, and the beginning of next week. Some storms on Thursday may produce gusty winds or excessive rainfall. Mebane is still facing significant challenges after Tropical Storm Chantal caused flooding earlier this week as storms come through the area again. Non-essential businesses are still being ordered to remain closed, and people are being told to limit their water usage amid a water shortage caused by Chantal. Mebane has declared its “Water Shortage Response Plan—Declaration of Rationing Stage V mandatory restrictions,” which go into effect immediately. The Graham–Mebane Water Treatment Plant was inundated with flooding from the Graham-Mebane Lake and its connecting tributaries as a result of Chantal, leading to the plant being unable to operate. City officials said the damage to the treatment plant is significant. “The pump building controls were flooded out … About six feet of water in the building … It basically shut down all pumping capabilities into the plant to treat water and also into the distribution system,” Mebane Public Utilities Director Kyle Smith said. The city says that the plant is still under repair and that Mebane has less than two days of drinking water left at the rate of usage. As a result, a water shortage has been declared and restrictions on water usage could remain in place for multiple days. Stage V restrictions are the highest level outlined in the city’s plan. Under those restrictions, “all industries, businesses, offices, and non-residential units” are to cease operations unless they fall into one of these categories: People in Mebane are being told not to use any water other than for limited drinking, limited restroom usage and required medical usage. Water should not be used for drinking if bottled water is available and showers are not considered to be a part of limited restroom usage. Mebane says the restrictions will be enforced by city personnel and law enforcement. The restrictions will remain in place until the plant is once again operating, and there is no current estimate as to when that will be. The city has received bottled water for distribution and is working to identify sites to do so. Mebane is under a state of emergency. However, there is no boil water advisory in place currently. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to FOX8 WGHP.
